context:
open scoped Classical
variable {α : Type*} [Group α]
stmt: theorem stmt (s : Subgroup α) : Nat.card s ∣ Nat.card α
paper: Theorem (Lagrange). Let G be a finite group and H a subgroup of G. Then the order of H divides the order of G.

stmt: theorem stmt (a : K) (ha : a ≠ 0) : a ^ (Fintype.card K - 1) = 1
paper: Theorem (Fermat's little theorem, finite-field form). Let K be a finite field with q elements. Then every nonzero a in K satisfies a^(q-1) = 1.

context:
open Set
variable {α : Type*} [ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder α] [TopologicalSpace α] [OrderTopology α] [DenselyOrdered α]
variable {δ : Type*} [LinearOrder δ] [TopologicalSpace δ] [OrderClosedTopology δ]
stmt:
theorem stmt {a b : α} (hab : a ≤ b) {f : α → δ} (hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) :
    Icc (f a) (f b) ⊆ f '' Icc a b
paper: Theorem (Intermediate value theorem). Let f : [a,b] -> R be continuous, with a <= b. Then for every y with f(a) <= y <= f(b) there is c in [a,b] with f(c) = y.

stmt: theorem stmt (n : ℕ) : ∃ p, n ≤ p ∧ Nat.Prime p
paper: Theorem (Euclid). There are infinitely many prime numbers; that is, for every natural number n there is a prime p with p >= n.

stmt: theorem stmt (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] : ((p - 1)! : ZMod p) = -1
paper: Theorem (Wilson). If p is a prime, then (p-1)! ≡ -1 (mod p).

stmt:
theorem stmt (f : ℝ → ℝ) {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (hfc : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b))
    (hfd : DifferentiableOn ℝ f (Ioo a b)) : ∃ c ∈ Ioo a b, deriv f c = (f b - f a) / (b - a)
paper: Theorem (Mean value theorem). Let a < b and let f be continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b). Then there is c in (a,b) with f'(c) = (f(b) - f(a)) / (b - a).

context:
open Filter Topology Bornology
variable {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X] [ProperSpace X] {s : Set X}
stmt:
theorem stmt (hs : IsBounded s) {x : ℕ → X} (hx : ∀ n, x n ∈ s) :
    ∃ a ∈ closure s, ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ Tendsto (x ∘ φ) atTop (𝓝 a)
paper: Theorem (Bolzano-Weierstrass). Every bounded sequence in R^n has a convergent subsequence, whose limit lies in the closure of the set containing the sequence.

stmt:
theorem stmt {G : Type*} [Group G] [Fintype G] (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] (hdvd : p ∣ Fintype.card G) :
    ∃ x : G, orderOf x = p
paper: Theorem (Cauchy). Let G be a finite group and p a prime dividing the order of G. Then G contains an element of order p.

context:
open EuclideanGeometry
variable {V : Type*} {P : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [MetricSpace P] [NormedAddTorsor V P]
stmt:
theorem stmt (p₁ p₂ p₃ : P) :
    dist p₁ p₃ * dist p₁ p₃ = dist p₁ p₂ * dist p₁ p₂ + dist p₃ p₂ * dist p₃ p₂ ↔
      ∠ p₁ p₂ p₃ = Real.pi / 2
paper: Theorem (Pythagoras and its converse). For points A, B, C in a Euclidean space, AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2 if and only if the angle ABC is a right angle.

stmt:
theorem stmt (hp : p ≠ 2) (hq : q ≠ 2) (hpq : p ≠ q) :
    legendreSym q p * legendreSym p q = (-1) ^ (p / 2 * (q / 2))
paper: Theorem (Quadratic reciprocity). Let p and q be distinct odd primes, and let (a/p) denote the Legendre symbol. Then (p/q)(q/p) = (-1)^(((p-1)/2)((q-1)/2)).

stmt: theorem stmt {f : ℂ[X]} (hf : 0 < degree f) : ∃ z : ℂ, IsRoot f z
paper: Theorem (Fundamental theorem of algebra). Every non-constant polynomial with complex coefficients has a complex root.

stmt: theorem stmt (x y : F) : |inner ℝ x y| ≤ ‖x‖ * ‖y‖
paper: Theorem (Cauchy-Schwarz). For vectors x, y in a real inner product space, |<x, y>| <= ||x|| ||y||.
